Subject: Tail-latency attribution & token-path drill request

Team —

AcmeHealth reported a recurring tail-latency spike on their primary chat route over the past 48h. They sent a small sample export (attached) showing a concentration of high-latency responses clustered around specific token sequences and longer KV-cache warmups. They asked for a way in Console to: 1) quickly surface the top token sequences contributing to 95th/99th percentile latency, 2) attribute cost and latency to tenant + route, and 3) drill from a heatmap into raw token paths and trace IDs so SREs can pull logs/trace payloads.

Ask: can we scope a lightweight investigative UI we can ship to tenants as a beta: a three-panel drill (time-series latency + cost delta, token-path heatmap, top offending traces with trace IDs and export)? Key constraints: must respect retention/K-anon policy, sampling should be configurable per-tenant, and exports must redact PII.

Please reply with:
- Diego: feasibility and rough infra effort (sampling, storage, trace linkage)
- Marissa: quick UI sketch and minimum viable interactions
- Lauren: runbook changes + retention/cost guidance
- Rishi: any SLA/fallback considerations (auto-fallback to shorter model or cached variant)

I copied Beth so they can confirm scope. Acme asking if we can provide an investigator view within 2 weeks (beta). Not asking for a full product rollout — just a diagnostic surface and exportable CSV with trace ids.

Thanks,
Hannah

Subject: Re: Tail-latency attribution & token-path drill request

Thanks Hannah — good writeup. High level: doable, with a couple of tradeoffs.

Proposal sketch:
- Instrumentation: attach a token-path-hash and a trace-id to inference logs for requests flagged as potential tails. Sampling: add adaptive tail-sampling that triggers denser capture for requests above p95; store token-path aggregates (hashed/tokenized) for 14 days by default.
- Storage: keep aggregated heatmaps per (tenant,route,window) rather than full token payloads to reduce cost. For traces we keep a short-lived trace payload (48–72h) and store pointers (trace-id) in the investigator UI for export.
- API surface: new /observability/paths endpoint that returns heatmap + top traces; will include flags for sample_rate and anonymize=true.

Estimated effort: 3 wks infra + 1.5 wks API + 1 wk frontend for an MVP if we parallelize. If we want faster (2 weeks) we can scope to a manual export flow only: surface top-token buckets in Console but send trace export to SREs via email/drive.

I created a stub Jira: OBS-9123 for infra work.

Diego

Looping in quick UI thoughts. I mocked a minimal investigator canvas and attached a screenshot. High-level interaction:
- Left panel: selectable time-series (latency p50/p95/p99 and cost deltas) with brush to select window.
- Center: token-path heatmap where x-axis is token position, y-axis is token cluster (common substrings) and intensity = aggregated latency contribution. Hover reveals sample token-hash + count.
- Right: top traces table with trace-id, tenant, route, duration, and an \"Open inLogs\" action that links to trace payload (respecting redaction).

MVP scope (sprint-friendly): heatmap + traces table + export CSV button. Add tenant-level sample-rate toggle in settings to control cost. If product agrees, prioritize in UX sprint-2 and we can ship a gated beta to Acme.

Attached: mock-heatmap-panel.png

Subject: Re: Tail-latency attribution & token-path drill request

Quick runbook and ops notes:

- Retention: keep aggregated heatmaps for 30 days by default; full trace payloads accessible for 72h. Acme asked for 7d access — that's possible but will increase storage costs ~2–3x. Need explicit approval.
- Redaction: token contents must be tokenized+hashed for investigator view. Provide explicit \"Request raw trace\" workflow that triggers a gated export with customer consent and audit log entry.
- Cost control: add tenant-level sampling slider (0.1%–5%) and an emergency toggle for SREs to raise sample rate for a window.
- SLA fallback: Rishi, we should define automatic fallback to the cached variant or smaller model when p99 latency crosses threshold for >2min. Also we need a metric alert to create an OBS incident to avoid noisy toggles.

I'll update the runbook doc and link to OBS-9123. From an ops perspective we can support a gated beta to Acme if they accept the default retention and sampling suggested above.

Lauren
